newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices firm on lower crop estimates.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices firm on lower crop estimates.

text.p: Indian cotton prices firmed on Tuesday cheered by lower crop estimates announced by the official Cotton Advisory Board, dealers said.

The board, at a meeting late on Monday, estimated the new crop for 1996-97 season at 15.50 million bales (170 kg each). Seasonal rains and a cyclone in producing centres forced the board to lower crop estimates, dealers said.

Traders had estimated the new crop at 16.50-17.00 million bales. In spot deals Bengal desi was quiet at 805/840 rupees per maund (37.32 kg), while Punjab sawginned was steady at 1,360/1,615 rupees. The cotton market is closed on Wednesday for Christmas will reopen for normal trading on Thursday.
